articles.title: Musculoskeletal ultrasound in traumatic emergencies: what radiologists need to know.
articles.abstract: While conventional radiography (CR) and computed tomography (CT) remain diagnostic staples in emergency settings, ultrasound (US) is a critical tool offering a rapid, dynamic, and noninvasive alternative for acute musculoskeletal (MSK) pathologies assessment. Prompt identification of conditions such as unstable fractures, soft tissue or muscular hematomas, joint effusions, and tendon ruptures is essential to prevent or mitigate long-term patient morbidity. This review summarizes the role of US in the emergency department, providing a practical overview of targeted scanning techniques and key sonographic signs. Additionally, common diagnostic pitfalls and effective escalation pathways are discussed to streamline clinical decision-making and optimize timely patient management.

articles.title: Providing Effective Feedback in the Current Fast-paced Hybrid Clinical Learning Environment.
A unified and domain-robust framework enables controllable multimodal brain MRI synthesis.
articles.abstract: Multimodal magnetic resonance image (MRI) synthesis can shorten examinations, reduce cost, and furnish contrasts that are difficult or impossible to acquire, but current models remain hard to control and brittle to shifts in scanner, protocol, and pathology. We present a unified, domain-robust synthesis framework that modulates spatial carriers with physically informed, domain-stable statistical guidance. A balanced soft-plus-hard conditioning scheme enables a single model to perform diverse contrast mapping, while allowing smooth user adjustment of contrast weighting. Evaluated on 991 test subjects from five public and three private datasets spanning cross-dataset, cross-protocol, and related cross-pathology scenarios, our approach matches or outperforms advanced baselines for both in-domain synthesis and inference under unseen domains without finetuning. Clinician Turing test and downstream glioma grading experiments further indicate realistic appearance, preservation of pathology-relevant information, and potential practical value under clinically heterogeneous conditions. By jointly delivering controllability, robustness to real-world variability, and physically informed, domain-stable guidance within one architecture, this work advances MRI synthesis toward deployment in heterogeneous clinical environments.

articles.title: Streamline pathology foundation model by cross-magnification distillation.
articles.abstract: Foundation models (FM) have transformed computational pathology but remain computationally prohibitive for clinical deployment due to their massive parameter counts and high-magnification processing requirements. Here, we introduce XMAG, a lightweight FM developed through cross-magnification distillation that transfers knowledge from a state-of-the-art 20x magnification teacher to an efficient 5x magnification student architecture. XMAG employs a compact backbone and operates entirely at 5x, requiring 11.3 times fewer patches per whole slide image (WSI) compared to existing approaches. Our novel distillation framework incorporates dual-level knowledge transfer, aligning both global image representations and local spatial features across magnification levels through carefully designed projection heads and spatial token mapping. We trained XMAG on 3.49 million images curated from publicly available datasets and evaluated performance across seven clinically relevant histopathology analysis tasks spanning multiple cancer types. Across four WSI-level classification tasks, XMAG achieved an average AUC within 1% of substantially larger foundation models while delivering up to 29.5-fold faster encoder-level processing, corresponding to an encoder throughput of 8.8 WSIs per minute in a controlled patch-encoding benchmark. We also found that performance differences remained task-dependent, with larger gaps observed for fine-grained tasks such as ISUP grading and patch-level phenotyping. We further explore end-to-end XMAG training as a direction for task-specific adaptation of the compact model. These results suggest that cross-magnification distillation is a promising strategy for developing efficient low-magnification pathology foundation models and may support more scalable WSI analysis in computationally constrained research and translational settings.

articles.title: CoilDrop-MRI: Self-supervised physics-guided MRI reconstruction with coil dropout.
articles.abstract: Self-supervised deep learning-based methods have shown great promise for accelerated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction, achieving high image quality without requiring fully sampled data for training. These methods typically partition the acquired data into two disjoint subsets to construct input-target pairs for optimizing the reconstruction network. However, existing approaches perform this partition exclusively within the spatial frequency (k-space) domain, leaving the coil dimension unexplored. To enforce full exploitation of signal correlation across receiver coils, we propose CoilDrop-MRI, which applies coil-wise dropout to the input and uses the dropped data as training targets in a self-supervised framework. This method is integrated into unrolled architectures in both image-domain (SENSE) and k-space (SPIRiT) formulations. We further demonstrate its versatility by extending CoilDrop-MRI to multi-shot, phase-corrected diffusion MRI (dMRI) reconstruction. CoilDrop-MRI is extensively validated on multi-site, multi-field-strength (0.3T, 0.55T, and 3T), and multi-modality (T1-weighted, T2-weighted, T2-FLAIR, and dMRI) datasets and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art self-supervised methods, achieving quality comparable to supervised reconstruction methods without requiring fully sampled reference training data. Moreover, CoilDrop-MRI exhibits strong data efficiency and robust generalization across imaging conditions, establishing it as a practical and versatile framework for self-supervised parallel MRI reconstruction.

articles.title: SegSTRONG-C: Segmenting Surgical Tools Robustly On Non-adversarial Generated "Corruptions"- An EndoVis'24 Challenge.
articles.abstract: Surgical data science has seen rapid ad vancement with the excellent performance of end-to-end deep neural networks (DNNs). Despite their successes, DNNs have been proven susceptible to minor "corrup tions," substantially impairing the model's performance, introducing a major concern for the translation of cutting-edge technology, especially in high-stakes scenarios. We introduce the SegSTRONG-C challenge dedicated to better understanding model deterioration under unforeseen but plausible non-adversarial "corruption" and the capabilities of contemporary methods that seek to improve it. Built on a dataset generated through counterfactual robotic replay, SegSTRONG-C provides paired clean and "corrupted" samples, enabling reproducible evaluation of model robustness. Participants are challenged to train tool segmentation algorithms on "uncorrupted" data and evaluate them on "corrupted" test domains for the binary robot tool segmentation task. Through comprehensive baseline experiments and participating submissions from widespread community engagement, SegSTRONG-C reveals key themes for model failure and identifies promising directions for improving robustness. The performance of challenge winners, achieving an average 0.9394 DSC and 0.9301 NSD across the unreleased test sets with "corruption" types: bleeding, smoke, and low brightness. This highlights how prior knowledge, customized training strategies, and architectural choice can be leveraged to improve robustness. In conclusion, the SegSTRONG-C challenge has identified practical approaches for enhancing model robustness. However, most approaches rely on conventional techniques that have known limitations. Looking ahead, we advocate for expanding intellectual diversity and creativity in non-adversarial robustness beyond data augmentation, calling for new paradigms that enhance universal robustness to unforeseen "corruptions" to facilitate richer applications in surgical data science.

articles.title: A two-stage model combining clinical and delta-radiomics features for prognosis in high-grade gliomas after chemoradiotherapy: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of integrating pre-radiotherapy and mid-radiotherapy radiomics, temporal changes in tumor radiomics (delta radiomics) during chemoradiotherapy, and clinical variables into prognostic models for individualized overall survival (OS) prediction in patients with high-grade glioma (HGG). METHODS: A total of 143 patients with HGG who underwent standard chemoradiotherapy were retrospectively enrolled from two centers. Patients were divided into a training cohort (n = 116), in which 5-fold cross-validation was performed, and an external test cohort (n = 27). Radiomics features were extracted from pre-radiotherapy and mid-radiotherapy MRI scans, and delta radiomic features were calculated as the differences between the two timepoints. Feature selection was performed using elastic-net-based stability selection, and radiomics scores (Rad-scores) were generated for each selected feature set using Cox models. Rad-scores were subsequently combined with clinical variables in a random survival forest (RSF) model for OS prediction. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was performed to evaluate prognostic stratification. RESULTS: The combined model integrating clinical variables and delta radiomics achieved a C-index of 0.818 and 0.761 in the validation and external test cohorts, respectively, outperforming models based solely on radiomics or clinical features. In the external test cohort, time-dependent discrimination yielded 12-, 18-, 24- and 30-month OS AUCs of 0.842, 0.856, 0.796, and 0.943, and Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significant risk stratification (p = 0.002). CONCLUSION: The findings of this retrospective study suggest that integrating multi-timepoint radiomics, delta radiomics features, and clinical variables may facilitate OS prediction in patients with HGG following standard chemoradiotherapy. While promising, the exploratory findings require further validation in larger prospective cohorts, given the limited size of the external validation cohort and the absence of MGMT promoter methylation status from the main model.

Quantitative and qualitative magnetic resonance imaging-based analysis to predict postoperative disease progression in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common abdominal malignancies and the third leading cause of cancer-related death globally. Predicting the postoperative prognosis of HCC remains an important area of clinical research. Many qualitative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) indicators have been used for noninvasive and global assessment of HCC for diagnostic and prognostic purposes. However, the prognostic value of quantitative MRI parameters has not been extensively validated in multicenter cohorts. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to verify whether MRI-based imaging features could improve prognostic prediction in patients with HCC. We developed prognostic models to predict the progression-free survival (PFS) of patients with HCC. METHODS: In this multicenter cohort study, 203 patients diagnosed with early- to intermediate-stage HCC were divided into a training dataset and an external validation dataset. In addition to clinical indicators, the candidates included qualitative and quantitative MRI data. Three noninvasive models were developed: the Clinical Model, the Radiological Model, and the Combined Model. The patients were stratified according to the risk of disease progression. Model performance was assessed through discrimination and calibration analyses, decision curve analysis was performed, and a clinical application was designed. In addition, the subgroups at different stages of the disease were analyzed, and PFS was compared between the high- and low-risk groups. RESULTS: Prognostic nutritional index, tumor-feeding vessels, mosaic architecture and the signal enhancement ratio (SER) parameter were identified as independent predictors of disease progression in patients with HCC. The Combined Model demonstrated superior performance compared with the Clinical and Radiological Models. The areas under the curve (AUCs) in the training dataset were 0.822, 0.748, and 0.795, whereas those in the validation dataset were 0.819, 0.758, and 0.677, respectively. The Combined Model also demonstrated favorable calibration and greater net clinical benefit on decision curve analysis. Its predictive ability remained consistent regardless of the Child-Pugh classification or Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer stage. CONCLUSION: This study highlights the important role of quantitative and qualitative MRI assessments in evaluating the prognosis of patients with HCC and emphasizes the predictive value of SER parameter. However, these findings should nevertheless be interpreted with caution given the relatively limited sample size, despite the use of bootstrap internal validation and external validation.

articles.title: Periprostatic adipose tissue imaging in prostate cancer: Imaging phenotypes, task-specific spatial strategies, and multicompartment integration-a critical review.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To appraise how periprostatic adipose tissue (PPAT) is defined, sampled, and evaluated in prostate cancer imaging, with emphasis on spatial strategy, intended clinical use, evidence maturity, and imaging-tissue correspondence. METHOD: We conducted a structured critical review with evidence mapping, supported by PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science searches through August 29, 2026, supplemented by prespecified Google Scholar and citation searches. Two reviewers independently screened records. Reports were mapped by imaging strategy, spatial target, clinical task, evaluation design, reproducibility, cohort overlap, and imaging-tissue correspondence. RESULTS: The formal evidence set comprised 113 reports, including 63 clinical imaging reports. Strategies comprised morphometry / computed tomography (CT) attenuation (48 reports), tissue-property / compositional imaging (4), PPAT-focused radiomics (4), and interface / multicompartment modelling (7). Quantitative reproducibility was reported in 19/63 clinical reports. Only two reports underwent independent external evaluation, and neither evaluated a PPAT-only model. Biological and translational evidence supported PPAT as a heterogeneous tumour-adjacent compartment, whereas direct spatially matched imaging-tissue validation remained uncommon. Clinical evidence spanned prebiopsy risk refinement, upgrading or active-surveillance reclassification, local extension and surgical planning, prognosis, treatment-related outcomes, and nodal and metastatic assessment; most reports lacked independent evaluation. CONCLUSIONS: PPAT imaging is best regarded as a set of spatially defined, task-specific phenotypes rather than a single biomarker. Current evidence positions PPAT as a candidate adjunct to established clinical and intraprostatic imaging information. Clinical adoption will require reproducible definitions and measurements, task-matched assessment of incremental value, independent external evaluation, and prospective evidence of decision impact.

Concept-Based Explainable AI in Retinal Imaging: Core Concepts, Techniques, and Challenges.
articles.abstract: In high-stakes domains like healthcare, establishing trust in AI-assisted decisions is critical for fostering confidence among experts and researchers. However, standard explanation methods may not fully meet clinical needs, offering raw data, such as saliency maps, rather than human-readable text and auditable, transparent reasoning. To bridge this gap, researchers are increasingly adopting concept-based approaches that express model reasoning through human-readable concepts grounded in expert-backed clinical knowledge. Although this field has advanced rapidly in recent years, retinal C-XAI remains methodologically heterogeneous, with limited agreement on taxonomy, evaluation, and clinical validation. This review identifies recurring reliability gaps in retinal C-XAI and synthesises potential directions for addressing them, including independent concept-level auditing, robustness testing, and clinician-informed validation. As an illustrative example, we discuss how the established SMILE methodology could be adapted for concept-level auditing in retinal C-XAI; this is presented as a candidate research direction rather than a new or clinically validated framework.

articles.title: Clinical Usability Evaluation of CT Work Systems: A Narrative Review and Socio-Technical Implementation Framework.
articles.abstract: Computed tomography (CT) services are commonly evaluated using image quality, radiation dose, and equipment uptime. These metrics, however, do not establish whether CT work systems can be used safely, efficiently, and consistently across clinical information flows. This review synthesizes usability standards, human factors concepts, and radiology informatics evidence to support clinical evaluation of CT work systems. The scope included scanner interfaces, RIS/PACS/EMR links, dose monitoring tools, protocol repositories, and workflow logs. We conducted a transparent narrative review using targeted PubMed/MEDLINE and IEEE Xplore searches, Crossref metadata checks, standards, guidance documents, and citation chaining. Evidence was organized by context of use, information system component, risk-relevant task, evaluation method, and implementation action. CT usability is a socio-technical property linking users, tasks, scanner interfaces, information systems, protocol governance, maintenance, and organizational context. No single method captures this system adequately. Digital timestamps and observation reveal workflow delays, while task-based testing and scales characterize interface performance and user burden. Protocol, dose monitoring, and maintenance audits identify lifecycle risks. The proposed framework maps five domains to evaluation methods, candidate indicators, mitigation strategies, and minimum reporting items. Comprehensive CT usability assessment should extend beyond global satisfaction and equipment performance. It should determine whether specified users can complete defined CT tasks within defined clinical and informatics contexts. Future research should validate CT-specific task libraries, usability scales, interoperable log definitions, and multi-site reporting standards.

articles.title: Use of Machine Learning and Imaging to Predict Outcomes After Lumbar Spine Surgery: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Postoperative outcomes following lumbar spine surgery remain variable, and existing clinical risk stratification methods offer limited predictive accuracy. Advances in machine learning enable quantitative analysis of routinely acquired spinal imaging, creating opportunities to improve preoperative outcome prediction. However, the methodological quality and clinical readiness of imaging-based machine learning models in lumbar spine surgery have not been systematically evaluated. This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched through October 2025 for studies using machine learning models trained on imaging data (MRI, CT, or radiographs) to predict postoperative outcomes after lumbar spine surgery. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool (PROBAST). Twenty-six studies published between 2019 and 2025 met inclusion criteria. Most models predicted patient-reported or clinical outcomes, with fewer addressing complications, structural outcomes, or imaging-derived biomarkers. MRI was the predominant modality. Model discrimination was frequently moderate to high (median AUC, 0.83), though external validation and calibration reporting were uncommon. All studies demonstrated high risk of bias, primarily related to analysis and validation practices. Imaging-based machine learning models show promise for improving preoperative outcome prediction after lumbar spine surgery, but methodological limitations limit current clinical applicability. Greater emphasis on external validation, standardized outcomes, and prospective evaluation is needed to support safe translation into routine spine care.

articles.title: Mitigating Domain Shift and Dataset Bias in Deep Learning Models for Cancer Diagnostics.
articles.abstract: The translation of deep learning architectures from controlled experimental settings into real-world cancer diagnostics is heavily bottlenecked by domain shift and demographic bias. While models routinely achieve near-perfect retrospective performance on internal datasets, validation across external multicenter cohorts incurs a systemic and severe performance degradation, with an average metric drop of 0.16 AUC. This review provides a comprehensive metasynthesis of contemporary algorithmic mitigation paradigms designed to alleviate distribution discrepancies, evaluating techniques ranging from classical stain normalization and adversarial feature alignment to test-time adaptation and large-scale self-supervised pathology foundation models. Our analysis reveals a critical dichotomy between raw diagnostic performance and algorithmic equity: current optimization frameworks that successfully elevate aggregate macro metrics frequently do so by obscuring or actively exacerbating underlying demographic and subpopulation disparities. To achieve safe, equitable, and universally reliable clinical artificial intelligence, the field must transcend static validation habits. We outline a future roadmap anchored on three critical axes: establishing intersectional disparity indices as primary regulatory endpoints, standardizing multivendor metadata-rich benchmarks, and prioritizing.

articles.title: Foundation Models and Multimodal Learning for Medical Data with Applications in Oncology.
articles.abstract: The rapid expansion of medical data, including radiological imaging, digital pathology, molecular profiling, electronic health records, and longitudinal clinical narratives, has created new opportunities for AI in healthcare, while also exposing the limitations of traditional unimodal modeling approaches. Multimodal learning addresses these challenges by integrating heterogeneous data sources, and recent advances in foundation models, large-scale pretrained models designed for broad task transfer, have further accelerated this shift. Together, these developments have given rise to multimodal foundation models that aim to learn generalizable, aligned representations across diverse clinical modalities. In this review, we provide an overview of multimodal foundation models in medical AI, with a particular focus on oncology. We first outline key medical data modalities and the machine learning objectives that motivate multimodal integration, including predictive, representational, and alignment-based goals. We then examine core architectural design patterns and training paradigms underlying multimodal foundation models, such as modality-specific encoders, fusion strategies, attention mechanisms, contrastive pretraining, and scalable self-supervised learning. Building on this foundation, we survey representative multimodal models across radiology, pathology, clinical text, and molecular domains. We further review applications of multimodal foundation models across the cancer care continuum, including early detection, diagnosis and subtyping, prognosis, therapy response prediction, and longitudinal survival modeling. Finally, we discuss critical challenges that limit clinical translation, including cross-institutional heterogeneity, temporal misalignment across modalities, weak supervision, interpretability, regulatory constraints, and workflow integration, and outline future directions for advancing safe and effective deployment in real-world oncology practice.

articles.title: Comparative Evaluation of Open-Weight Large Language Models for Pathological Brain MRI Reports Classification: From Prompts to a Fine-Tuned Model.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Automated semantic classification of radiology reports can enhance clinical workflows and research, but often relies on language- and task-specific models, limiting scalability. This study aims to evaluate and improve the 0-shot baseline performance of open-weight large language models (LLMs) in the semantic classification of free-text magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reports. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A corpus of 1385 reports from a single neuroradiology center was used to assess four LLMs (GPT-OSS-20B, Magistral-Small-2509, Gemma-4-31B, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B) of comparable scale (∼20-35B parameters). The brain MRI reports were labeled as Pathological or Non-Pathological, with the Pathological ones further classified into five diagnostic categories (Neoformation, Vascular, Inflammation/Infection, Neurodegenerative, Other). The LLMs were evaluated using zero- and few-shot prompting with majority-vote aggregation. Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA) fine-tuning was then applied to the best-performing model across multiple configurations. Performance was assessed using Macro F1, Micro F1, Precision, Recall, and Exact Match Accuracy. RESULTS: The binary classification task achieved a Macro F1 score of 0.84 on the best-performing Qwen3.5-35B-A3B model, while multilabel classification reached 0.81. Majority voting (MV) outperformed individual-set predictions. QLoRA fine-tuning yielded a Macro F1 score of 0.83 on the multilabel task; the improvement over the 0-shot baseline was statistically supported for Macro F1, Micro F1, Macro Precision, and Exact Match, whose bootstrap 95% confidence intervals excluded zero, but not for Macro Recall. Fine-tuning and few-shot prompting strategies are complementary, with neither consistently outperforming the other. Error analysis showed that the models struggled with borderline annotation cases and often missed secondary labels. CONCLUSION: Open-weight LLMs demonstrate strong capability for neuroradiology report classification without extensive task-specific training. Fine-tuning further improves performance, supporting integration into scalable semantic radiology data pipelines. However, the present evidence comes from a single Italian center without external validation, and the fine-tuning gain was estimated on a small held-out test set, for which the Macro F1 improvement, though statistically significant, has a confidence interval with a lower bound close to zero. In this light, the approach is best positioned as an internal indexing and semantic-retrieval tool, supporting faster report retrieval, structured cohort identification, internal audit, and scalable phenotyping for neuroradiology research and data warehousing, as well as efficient active-learning strategies, with broader generalizability requiring additional external multicentre validation before clinical deployment.

articles.title: Repeated metastasis-directed radiotherapy in patients with oligorecurrent prostate cancer: outcomes and risk stratification from a large multinational PSMA PET-guided cohort.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Repeated metastasis-directed radiotherapy (MDRT) is increasingly used in patients with metachronous oligometastatic prostate cancer. However, the efficacy and optimal patient selection criteria remain insufficiently defined. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Within the multinational PORTAL consortium, we evaluated outcomes of repeated MDRT in patients with PSMA-PET-detected oligorecurrent hormone-sensitive prostate cancer undergoing ≥ 2 MDRT cycles. The primary endpoint was androgen deprivation therapy-free survival (ADT-FS), secondary endpoints included polymetastatic-free survival, next-line systemic therapy-free survival, and overall survival, all calculated from start of repeated MDRT. A multivariable Cox regression model was developed to predict ADT-FS, and its performance was evaluated by bootstrapped internal validation using discrimination (C-index) and calibration. RESULTS: A total of 177 patients were included. Median follow-up after second MDRT was 26.1 months. During follow-up, 86 patients initiated ADT, 59 developed polymetastatic disease, 38 received next-line systemic therapy, and 17 deaths occurred. Two-year ADT-FS was 50.2 % (95 % CI 41.4-58.3). Two-year polymetastatic-free, next-line systemic therapy-free, and overall survival were 64.4 % (95 % CI 55.4-72.0), 83.5 % (95 % CI 76.0-88.9), and 94.2 % (95 % CI 88.2-97.2), respectively. In the multivariable Cox regression model, a longer interval between first and second MDRT (HR 0.96 per month, 95 % CI 0.94-0.99; p = 0.003) and treatment of a single versus ≥ 2 new lesions (HR for ≥ 2 lesions 1.88, 95 % CI 1.22-2.90; p = 0.006) were independently associated with ADT-FS. Model discrimination was moderate (optimism-corrected C-index 0.68) with good calibration. CONCLUSIONS: In this multicentre cohort of patients with PSMA PET-detected metachronous oligorecurrent prostate cancer undergoing repeated MDRT, favourable ADT-FS outcomes were observed, with approximately half of patients remaining ADT-free two years after second MDRT. Given the absence of a comparator group, these outcomes may reflect both the effects of treatment and favourable disease biology of patients who remained eligible for repeated MDRT. The interval between MDRT cycles, and the number of metastases, independently predicted ADT-FS and may support patient selection.

articles.title: Selective lipid Metabolic remodelling in radiosensitive normal tissues after FLASH radiotherapy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: FLASH radiotherapy, delivered at ultra-high dose rates, spares normal tissues while maintaining tumor control, but the molecular basis of this differential response remains poorly defined, particularly at timepoints relevant to tissue repair. We investigated whether lipid metabolism contributes to the FLASH effect in head and neck cancer. MATERIALS AND METHODS: MOC2 tumor-bearing mice received a single 10 Gy fraction of conventional (CONV) or ultra-high dose-rate FLASH protons, with non-irradiated controls (CTRL). Tongue and contralateral tumors were collected two weeks later and analyzed by bulk lipidomics, spatial lipidomics and proteomics. After biochemical filtering, 1,547 lipid species across 37 classes were quantified. RESULTS: At two weeks, CONV irradiation was associated with a triglyceride-catabolic, oxidative-stress signature in tongue tissue, marked by loss of the lipid-droplet hydrolase Ces1d alongside induction of the peroxisomal β-oxidation enzyme Acox1. FLASH irradiation was instead associated with a distinct lipid-remodelling signature: suppression of Mgll, induction of Apoe, membrane phospholipid remodelling (increased phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidylethanolamine), and Lypla2 upregulation. Spatial lipidomics provided illustrative spatial context consistent with concentration of these changes in minor salivary gland acini. Tumor tissue showed no comparable modality-specific divergence. CONCLUSIONS: These correlative multi-omics data indicate that FLASH is associated with remodelling of lipid metabolism in radiosensitive normal tissue, beyond a simple reduction of acute oxidative damage. We propose a Lipid Metabolic Remodelling Hypothesis for testing: the remodelling of lipid metabolism observed after FLASH may contribute to normal-tissue sparing rather than representing solely a downstream consequence of reduced acute oxidative damage. This model complements existing physicochemical models and offers a basis for radioprotection strategies in head and neck radiotherapy.

articles.title: Multi-center comparison of relative stopping power estimation of an ex vivo phantom using clinical X-ray CT scanners and a proton CT prototype.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Accurate estimation of relative stopping power (RSP) is essential for proton therapy (PT) treatment planning. Emerging X-ray computed tomography (xCT) technologies are enabling more advanced RSP calibration strategies, but may also introduce greater variability across centers. This study aimed to assess inter-center variability in xCT calibration and RSP estimation for proton treatment planning, using a proton CT (pCT) prototype as reference. MATERIAL AND METHODS: An ex vivo phantom was transported to five European PT centers and one research center, and scanned with both single-energy and dual-energy xCT systems. Acquisitions were performed in three phantom configurations, simulating different anatomical sizes. The reconstructed xCT images were calibrated to RSP according to each center's clinical protocol and compared against the pCT-derived RSP maps. RESULTS: Voxel-by-voxel comparison between xCT-based and pCT-based RSP maps showed inter-center RSP variability of about 1% in soft tissues and up to 5% in bone, with larger differences observed for larger phantom sizes. The largest discrepancies (up to 5%) relative to pCT were observed in the same configurations. Centers implementing beam-hardening corrections generally showed closer agreement with pCT, whereas the effect of size-specific HLUTs was tissue- and anatomy-dependent. The impact of these RSP variations on water-equivalent thickness in representative clinical scenarios resulted in a 2σ inter-center variability of 1.09% and 1.39% for brain and prostate cases, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: This work presents the first inter-center comparison of xCT-based RSP estimation using an ex vivo phantom and pCT measurements as reference. The observed variability highlights the relevance of a comprehensive and standardized validation of xCT calibration protocols.

articles.title: Efficacy of Radiofrequency Combined with Chemical Sympatholysis in the Treatment of Primary Palmar Hyperhidrosis: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate and compare the efficacy and safety of radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RFT) and combined with chemical sympatholysis (RFT-CS) for the treatment of primary palmar hyperhidrosis (PPH) (Hyperhidrosis Disease Severity Scale [HDSS] grade III or IV). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients who underwent computed tomography-guided percutaneous thoracic sympathetic neurolysis (TSN) for PPH were retrospectively analyzed and divided into two treatment regimens: RFT (group RFT, N = 60, 120 sides) and RFT combined with CS (group RFT-CS, N = 58, 116 sides). RESULTS: At 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months, the number of sides with HDSS III/IV in the RFT group was 29, 32, 41, 47, and 56, respectively; in the RFT-CS group, 25, 31, 36, 40, and 45, with no statistically significant intergroup differences at any time point (all P ≥ .05). Overall recurrence rates rose from 3.0% at 1 month to 19.5% at 24 months, with no significant differences between groups at any time point (all P ≥ .05). The RFT-CS group had significantly higher compensatory hyperhidrosis (CH) rates at 12 months (62.1% vs. 56.7%; P = .012) and 24 months (58.6% vs. 50.0%; P = .014), and a higher incidence of thoracic neuralgia at 1 month (P = .023) and 3 months (P = .011). CONCLUSION: Both of the TSN treatment modes are effective for the treatment of severe PPH. Compared with RFT alone, RFT combined with CS does not seem to show better efficacy but increases the occurrence of CH and thoracic neuralgia.

articles.title: Intra-Articular Injection Use and Total Knee Arthroplasty After Genicular Artery Embolization for Knee Osteoarthritis: A Matched National Claims Analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To characterize intra-articular injection use before and after genicular artery embolization (GAE) for knee osteoarthritis (OA) and to compare progression to total knee arthroplasty (TKA) with matched knee OA patients. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the Merative MarketScan Commercial and Medicare Supplemental databases, 2014-2024. Patients undergoing GAE for knee OA were identified by CPT code 37242 with a knee OA diagnosis within 7 days, excluding non-OA indications. Annualized steroid and any intra-articular injection use was compared for the 12 months before and 6 months after GAE. Progression to TKA at 6 and 12 months was analyzed against non-GAE knee OA patients matched 10:1 on age, sex, region, index year, and baseline injection frequency. RESULTS: Of 436 patients with GAE for knee OA, 126 met enrollment criteria for the injection analysis (mean age, 64.2 years; 57.9% female). Mean annualized steroid injection use decreased from 0.96 to 0.48 per patient-year (-50.4%; P = .004) and any intra-articular injection from 2.88 to 1.60 (-44.4%; P < .001). Among 52 baseline steroid injection users, 36 (69.2%) stopped and 46 (88.5%) had fewer injections. TKA did not differ from matched comparators at 6 months (5.8% vs 6.8%; P = .858) or 12 months (13.1% vs 12.8%; P = 1.000). CONCLUSION: Steroid injection use decreased after GAE, while early progression to TKA did not differ from matched comparators. Prospective studies with longer follow-up and clinical outcomes are needed to determine whether GAE reduces the need for injections or affects long-term TKA rates.

articles.title: Cross-scanner validation and time-stability analysis of STARE, a blood-free quantification tool for brain imaging with irreversible PET tracers.
articles.abstract: "Gold standard" blood-based quantification of dynamic 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) data has limited practical clinical applications due to cost and complexity of data collection and analysis. We previously presented a blood-free quantification alternative, STARE (Source-to-Target Automatic Rotating Estimation), that was validated on 18F-FDG data acquired on an ECAT EXACT HR+ scanner. Here, we extend that initial work by applying STARE to within-subject data acquired with both a Siemens Biograph mCT scanner and a portable Brain Biosciences CerePET scanner. Approach: Performance was assessed by comparing regional net influx rates (Ki) estimated using STARE and the standard blood-based Patlak approach. Twenty participants underwent 60-minute brain 18F-FDG scans, on two different days, once in each scanner. The time-stability of both STARE- and Patlak-based Ki estimates was evaluated by applying each method to the first 20 (STARE only), 30, 40, and 50 minutes of data. Main results: STARE demonstrated high correlation with Patlak Ki estimates, particularly in the Biograph mCT (r = 0.82-0.93 (within-region)), with lower correlation in the CerePET (r = 0.27-0.62 (within-region)). In the Biograph dataset, STARE showed small deviations from the 60-min estimates across all evaluated durations (20 min and above), whereas deviations increased with shorter durations in CerePET data. The Patlak approach showed smaller changes across abbreviated scan durations in both datasets. Significance: STARE shows potential as a noninvasive alternative to traditional blood-based quantification of dynamic 18F-FDG PET brain data, facilitating shorter, blood-free acquisition. This advancement could make dynamic 18F-FDG PET brain imaging more accessible and comfortable for patients, potentially facilitating broader clinical adoption. &#xD.

articles.title: A harmonisation framework for multi-centre preclinical PET imaging across a national research infrastructure.
articles.abstract: Quantitative preclinical positron emission tomography (PET) imaging plays an important role in translational research, yet variability across scanners, sites, and analysis workflows remains a major barrier to robust multi-centre studies. In this work, we developed and evaluated a harmonisation framework across a national network of preclinical PET facilities. Approach. Six identical NEMA NU~4-2008 image quality phantoms were manufactured and distributed to six sites, where they were imaged using local acquisition and reconstruction protocols across multiple scanner platforms.Main Results. Substantial variability in contrast recovery, uniformity, and spill-over ratios was observed under site-specific conditions. Centralised automated re-analysis produced only minor reductions in variability, indicating that inter-user effects were relatively small, compared to site-specific protocol variations. In contrast, optimisation of reconstruction parameters led to a marked reduction in inter-scanner variability (an average of 60\% reduction across larger rods), particularly for voxel-wise maximum contrast recovery coefficients (CRC_max^vox), which are more sensitive to noise and reconstruction settings than the standard axial averaging NEMA CRC metric. Following harmonisation, the variability of CRC_max^vox approached and was lower that of conventional axial-averaged NEMA analysis (CRC_max^avg), with reductions ranging 7--33\% across the 1--5 mm rods, demonstrating improved quantitative consistency even at the voxel level.Significance. These findings show that scanner and site-specific protocol variations are the dominant factors for harmonisation in preclinical PET. By systematically evaluating acquisition, image reconstruction and analysis related sources of variability across a national network of heterogeneous preclinical PET systems, this work provides a practical framework for harmonisation. The proposed framework is conceptually aligned with clinical harmonisation initiatives such as EARL and provides a practical basis for the future development of harmonised performance ranges across preclinical scanners. This enables more reliable multi-centre studies and supports the use of quantitative, voxel-wise imaging biomarkers in translational research.

articles.title: Spatial sampling for triaxial OPM-MEG: understanding neurodevelopmental trajectory.
articles.abstract: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) measures magnetic fields generated by current flow in neural assemblies, providing a non-invasive means to track brain function. In recent years, the MEG field has been revolutionised by a new class of field sensor called an Optically Pumped Magnetometer (OPM). OPMs are small, lightweight, and allow construction of wearable and reconfigurable arrays of 'triaxial' field sensors (that measure magnetic fields along three axes simultaneously). These systems can be used to capture MEG data across the life span, from infancy to adulthood. With such multi-axis sensing arrays coming into routine use, here we aimed determine how dense a sensor array is required to adequately capture the spatial variation of neuromagnetic fields across the scalp.Approach: We simulated neuromagnetic fields based on realistic head geometries of individuals aged 15 months to 34 years. We then used two independent approaches to determine the sensor spacing required to capture the highest spatial variation of the field across the scalp surface: one method was based on spherical harmonic decomposition of neuromagnetic fields, and the other based on evaluating sensor redundancy in densely sampled arrays.Main results: Both methods agree in showing that the required sensor separation increases with age, from ~40 mm in a 1-year-old to ~55 mm in an adult.Significance: The sensor spacings obtained in our simulations represent upper bounds in the required values: separations above these bounds will not adequately capture spatial field variation; however, continuing to reduce sensor separation below these limits will continue to improve performance. These findings are important for the future development of OPM-MEG technology, particularly the construction of systems for neurodevelopmental applications.

articles.title: Photon-counting CT based vestibular aqueduct trajectory analysis for the assessment of Ménière's disease endotypes and hearing loss.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ménière's disease (MD) is a heterogeneous inner ear disorder, and imaging-based endotype identification may inform prognosis and personalized management. The vestibular aqueduct (VA) is a candidate imaging biomarker, and photon-counting CT (PCCT) offers high-resolution depiction of temporal bone microanatomy. This study evaluated PCCT-derived VA morphometric parameters as imaging biomarkers for MD endotype identification and hearing loss assessment. METHODS: In this retrospective study, 106 patients (212 ears) underwent temporal bone PCCT and 3.0-T 3D-FLAIR MRI. PCCT parameters included angular trajectory of the VA (ATVA), VA visibility grade, morphologic subtype, midpoint width, VA length, and posterior semicircular canal-posterior fossa distance. Two neuroradiologists independently evaluated all images. Diagnostic performance for six clinically motivated tasks was assessed by AUC with leave-one-patient-out cross-validation (LOPOCV); associations with pure-tone average (PTA) were evaluated by multivariable linear regression with cluster-robust standard errors. RESULTS: Interobserver agreement was excellent (ICC, 0.84-0.91). VA visibility grading identified the hypoplastic endotype with an AUC of 0.860 (LOPOCV, 0.812); combined VA morphology and midpoint width distinguished the degenerated endotype with an AUC of 0.784 (LOPOCV, 0.736). Multivariable regression identified ATVA as an independent PTA predictor (β = 0.238, p = 0.023). CONCLUSIONS: PCCT-derived VA morphometric parameters enabled MD endotype identification despite clinical heterogeneity and were associated with hearing loss severity, supporting their potential role as imaging biomarkers for MD management.

articles.title: Quantitative ultrasound-derived estimated fat fraction for detection and grading of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in a pediatric population.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pediatric metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) prevalence is approximately 10%, but ultrasound fat quantification lacks validation. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of quantitative ultrasound-derived estimated fat fraction (USFF) against magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) in children with suspected MASLD. METHODS: This prospective single-center study enrolled 65 children aged 6-18 years with suspected MASLD. USFF, tissue attenuation imaging (TAI), tissue scatter distribution imaging (TSI), hepato-renal index (EzHRI), and shear wave elastography (SWE) were measured on a Samsung R10 Prestige platform; 3.0 T MRI-PDFF served as reference. Steatosis was graded using pediatric PDFF thresholds. Diagnostic performance was assessed by ROC analysis with DeLong comparisons and internally validated by bootstrap resampling; agreement by Bland-Altman analysis; inter-operator reproducibility assessed in a randomly selected 30-child subset. RESULTS: Among 65 children (48 boys; median age 11.2 years), 20 were classified as S0, 29 as S1, and 16 as S2-3. USFF AUCs were 0.941 (≥S1) and 0.960 (≥S2), higher than EzHRI and SWE, and similar to TAI (0.903, 0.957) and TSI (0.900, 0.880). USFF strongly correlated with MRI-PDFF (ρ = 0.906) but systematically underestimated PDFF (mean bias - 3.13%; non-parametric limits of agreement - 14.51% to + 4.24%). In an exploratory analysis, younger children (<12 years) showed larger bias (-4.00% vs - 1.82%, p = 0.029) with similar AUC point estimates. CONCLUSIONS: USFF shows high diagnostic performance (AUC > 0.94) for pediatric MASLD, but its 3.13% underestimation and wide non-parametric limits of agreement warrant caution. USFF may serve as a practical tool for categorical steatosis grading in children with suspected MASLD, and the proposed thresholds require external validation before clinical use.

articles.title: Microstructural assessment of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction using second-order motion-compensated spin echo diffusion tensor cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate myocardial microstructural alterations in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction using second-order motion-compensated spin echo cardiac diffusion tensor imaging (M2-cDTI), and to determine whether cDTI can reveal abnormalities beyond late gadolinium enhancement (LGE). MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this cross-sectional observational study, 41 patients with HCM and 21 healthy volunteers underwent 1.5 T CMR including cine, LGE, and M2-cDTI. All myocardial segments were categorised into three groups based on LGE characteristics, LGE-positive (signal intensity ≥ 6 standard deviations [SD] above reference myocardium-the relatively normal myocardium), LGE-grey (signal intensity 2-6 SD above reference myocardium), and LGE-negative (signal intensity < 2 SD above reference myocardium). RESULTS: Global analysis revealed significantly elevated second eigenvector angle (E2A) in the HCM group compared with controls (44.04° ± 3.49 vs. 39.54° ± 3.70, p < 0.001). Initial segment-level comparisons showed higher E2A and lower FA in LGE-positive segments, whereas LGE-grey and LGE-negative segments showed higher E2A and FA than control segments. After accounting for intra-patient clustering, LGE classification remained significantly associated with E2A, with higher estimated marginal mean E2A values in LGE-negative, LGE-grey and LGE-positive segments than in controls (42.21°, 43.80° and 44.73° vs. 39.72°, respectively; all adjusted p < 0.05; Table 3), whereas the regional differences in FA were no longer statistically significant (F = 2.58, p = 0.052). CONCLUSION: In vivo M2-cDTI may reveal altered myocardial diffusion characteristics in HCM, even in regions without evident LGE, highlighting its potential as a sensitive biomarker for early detection of myocardial abnormalities.

articles.title: Identification of symptomatic carotid atherosclerotic plaques using dual-layer spectral detector computed tomography-derived perivascular adipose tissue parameters and plaque morphology.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To establish and validate a multidimensional model for identifying symptomatic carotid plaques based on the combination of plaque morphological characteristics and perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) parameters obtained from dual-layer spectral detector computed tomography (DLCT). METHODS: This single-center study included 256 patients with carotid atherosclerosis. Patients were divided into symptomatic and asymptomatic groups based on the presence or absence of transient ischemic attack or ipsilateral ischemic stroke within 2 weeks before DLCT. The study comprised a retrospective training cohort (n = 133), a retrospective internal validation cohort (n = 58), and a prospectively enrolled independent temporal test cohort (n = 65). Conventional plaque characteristics and multiple PVAT parameters were compared between the two groups. Imaging variables independently associated with symptomatic carotid plaques were identified using multivariable logistic regression and incorporated into classification models. RESULTS: Degree of stenosis, plaque burden, and the effective atomic number (Zeff) of PVAT were independently associated with symptomatic carotid plaques. Model 2 incorporated all three parameters demonstrating strong discriminatory performance, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves of 0.907, 0.825, and 0.848 in the training, validation, and test sets, respectively. Incorporation of PVAT Zeff improved the discriminative performance and reclassification beyond conventional stenosis and plaque-burden assessment. CONCLUSIONS: Degree of stenosis, plaque burden, and PVAT Zeff were independently associated with symptomatic carotid plaques. Adding PVAT Zeff to conventional plaque characteristics improved model discrimination and provided complementary information for the characterization of symptomatic lesions.

articles.title: Deep learning-based super-resolution reconstruction for improved image quality in shoulder MRI.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare the image quality of shoulder Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) using three imaging acquisition or reconstruction approaches-Parallel Imaging (PI), Compressed Sensing (CS), and Deep Learning-Based Super-Resolution Reconstruction (SR)-and to evaluate reader-assessed image quality and preference. METHODS: A retrospective study included 60 patients (27 males, 33 females; mean age 53.67 ± 12.11 years). Shoulder MRI was performed with PI, CS and SR (reconstructed from CS data) across six sequences. Quantitative and qualitative assessments were conducted by experienced observers. Three radiologists selected clinically preferred sequences after a 2-week washout. Consistency and inter-group comparisons were statistically analyzed. RESULTS: The quantitative and qualitative assessment between observers showed good consistency. The SR group showed significantly higher quantitative measurements across all six sequences of structures [e.g. SNR: Supraspinatus tendon SR 14.03 (10.60, 20.26), CS 11.87 (8.39, 15.96), PI 8.75 (5.18, 13.51), P < 0.001] than PI and CS. SR images generally showed lower edge rise distance (ERD) values, significant overall differences among PI, CS, and SR (P < 0.01), Qualitative assessment revealed that SR overall differences among PI, CS and SR, with statistically significant differences (P < 0.001). Furthermore, three reader preference results indicated a preference for SR images that all readers preferred SR images (86 %, 92 %, and 93 %). CONCLUSION: Compared to PI and CS, SR significantly improves image quality in shoulder MRI without increasing acquisition time. SR enhances the visualization of fine anatomical structures, providing improved image quality and supporting its potential application in clinical shoulder MRI.

articles.title: Longitudinal hematoma resolution after burr-hole evacuation with adjunctive scepter mini-assisted middle meningeal artery embolization: A multicenter matched cohort study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the radiographic and clinical outcomes of adjunctive middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) performed with the Scepter Mini dual-lumen balloon microcatheter following burr-hole evacuation for chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH), and to explore the feasibility of characterizing distal embolic penetration using the proposed MMA Embolization Penetration Score (MMA-EPS). METHODS: This retrospective multicenter matched cohort study included consecutive patients with cSDH treated with burr-hole evacuation followed by adjunctive MMAE using the Scepter Mini and Onyx™ 18. A matched historical cohort treated with burr-hole evacuation alone served as controls. The primary endpoint was longitudinal hematoma thickness regression on serial computed tomography. Secondary endpoints included functional outcome, recurrence, all-cause mortality, and procedural safety. RESULTS: Twenty-two patients with 38 embolized cSDHs were compared with 22 matched controls comprising 38 cSDHs. All embolized hematomas achieved MMA-EPS Grade 3 or 4 and demonstrated complete radiographic resolution by 6 months, whereas residual hematoma persisted in controls (0.0 ± 0.0 vs. 0.7 ± 0.9 mm). Favorable functional outcome (mRS 0-2) at 6 months was achieved in 86.4% versus 45.5% of patients. Exploratory analyses showed numerically lower recurrence (4.5% vs. 13.6%) and all-cause mortality (0% vs. 13.6%) following MMAE; however, the study was not powered to assess differences in these endpoints. Technical success was achieved in all embolizations without major procedure-related complications. CONCLUSION: Adjunctive MMAE using the Scepter Mini dual-lumen balloon microcatheter was associated with accelerated hematoma resolution, improved functional recovery, and an excellent procedural safety profile compared with burr-hole evacuation alone.

articles.title: Paediatric thalamic tumours: a predictive MR phenotype.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To utilise MR phenotyping in accurately predicting paediatric thalamic tumour type via qualitative MR analysis and quantitative diffusion histogram analysis, with the aim of optimising pre-surgical planning and patient outcomes. METHODS: Patients with tumours epicentred in the thalamus were identified through an electronic patient record search (2000 to 2024). Radiological features evaluated included tumour margins, homogeneity, cystic components, T1 and T2 signal, contrast enhancement, and haemorrhage. Histopathological tumour type, WHO grade, and molecular subtype were recorded. Tumour masks incorporating both solid and cystic components were manually drawn on T2-weighted b0 images and ADC histograms were constructed and analysed. RESULTS: 34 patients (12 male, 22 female) were included, with a mean age of 10.4 years (range 2.4 months to 16 years). Diffuse midline gliomas (DMG) accounted for 24% and pilocytic astrocytomas (PA) for 28% of the cohort. Further tumour types included low-grade astrocytomas (9%), DNETs, PXAs, and embryonal tumours (8.8% each), with germinoma, glioblastoma, supratentorial ependymoma, ganglioglioma, lymphoma, and ATRT each comprising 3%. ADC p10 was significantly lower in DMG than PA (877 ± 152 vs. 1053 ± 152 × 10⁻⁶ mm²/s; t = 2.25, df = 13, p = 0.042, Cohen's d = 1.16). ADC mean showed a large but non-significant difference (p = 0.068). PAs were well-defined and microcystic with brush-like enhancement. DMGs were ill-defined with patchy enhancement, lower ADC values, and frequent susceptibility artefact. CONCLUSION: Distinctive qualitative and quantitative MR features, particularly ADC p10, can guide the neuroradiologist in predicting tumour type and informing the decision between safe maximal resection and biopsy-first surgical pathways.

articles.title: Contralateral DTI-ALPS index as a prognostic biomarker in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma: integrating extent of resection and sex-stratified analyses.
articles.abstract: AIM: This study aimed to evaluate the independent prognostic value of the contralateral DTI-ALPS index in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, incorporating tumor morphometry, extent of resection, and sex-stratified analyses within a multivariable framework. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on 153 IDH-wildtype glioblastoma patients from the publicly available UPENN-GBM dataset. Contralateral DTI-ALPS was calculated using DSI Studio via manual ROI placement; tumor morphometry was derived from expert-annotated segmentation labels using 3D Slicer. Survival analyses included Kaplan-Meier estimation, multivariable Cox regression, time-dependent ROC, restricted cubic spline, and sequential C-index comparison with likelihood-ratio testing. RESULTS: The contralateral DTI-ALPS index independently predicted overall survival after adjustment for age, sex, tumor volume, and GTR status (HR = 0.405, 95% CI: 0.227-0.725, p = 0.002). Each one standard deviation increase in DTI-ALPS was associated with a 24.2% reduction in mortality risk. GTR ≥ 90% (HR = 0.651, p = 0.017) and age (HR = 1.021, p = 0.007) also retained independent significance. DTI-ALPS significantly improved model discrimination beyond age alone (C-index: 0.625 → 0.653 → 0.668; likelihood-ratio test p = 0.002). Time-dependent AUC reached 0.741 at 6 months. ALPS-based stratification was more pronounced in the subtotal resection subgroup. Sex-stratified analyses showed numerically stronger associations in females, but formal interaction testing did not confirm effect modification. In an exploratory MGMT subset (n = 57), DTI-ALPS did not retain independent significance after MGMT adjustment. CONCLUSION: The contralateral DTI-ALPS index may provide complementary prognostic information beyond established clinical predictors in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma; however, given the incomplete MGMT methylation data and ongoing methodological debate regarding the biological validity of DTI-ALPS, these findings should be considered exploratory. Prospective validation in cohorts with complete molecular and treatment data is required.

articles.title: Detection frequency of cystic rhomboid lip in a nonoperative clinical population: an MR imaging morphologic study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The cystic rhomboid lip (CRL), a diverticular expansion of the fourth ventricular lateral recess at the foramen of Luschka, is familiar to posterior fossa surgeons but remains incompletely characterized on Magnetic Resonance (MR) imaging. We aimed to determine its MR imaging detection frequency and morphologic features in a nonoperative referral population and to evaluate a practical recognition framework against surgically confirmed cystic cerebellopontine angle (CPA) mimics. METHODS: In this retrospective 2-center study, 662 consecutive patients who underwent thin-section skull base MR imaging for suspected posterior fossa cranial nerve disorders (2022-2024) were independently reviewed by 2 neuroradiologists. Based on anatomic and surgical literature, CRL was defined a priori by two required features at the foramen of Luschka: anterior displacement of CN IX-X and posterior displacement of the choroid plexus (the CN-choroid plexus separation sign), with a CSF-equivalent signal in the intervening space. Ipsilateral lateral recess dilatation was considered a supportive but nonmandatory feature. Extension pattern was classified with a radiologic adaptation of the Akiyama framework. The same features were then assessed in 54 surgically and histopathologically confirmed cystic or solid-cystic lesions at the level of the lower cranial nerves. RESULTS: CRL was detected in 42/662 patients (6.3%; 95% CI, 4.7-8.5%), comprising 48 lesions (6 bilateral). Mean age was 55.8 ± 15.8 years; 61.9% were women. Mean maximum diameter was 15.7 ± 2.8 mm. A jugular foramen extension pattern (JFT) was present in 43/48 lesions (89.6%) and a lateral extension pattern (LET) in 5/48 (10.4%); JFT lesions were larger than LET lesions. Lateral recess dilatation was present in 32/48 lesions (66.7%). The CN-choroid plexus separation sign was present in 48/48 CRLs and in 0/54 comparison lesions. CSF-equivalent signal was present in 14/54 comparison lesions (25.9%), all arachnoid cysts accompanying a solid tumor, none of which showed the separation sign. Interobserver agreement was perfect for CRL detection (κ = 1.00) and extension pattern (κ = 1.00) and excellent for diameter measurements (ICC, 0.91-0.93). CONCLUSION: CRL is a relatively common finding on thin-section skull base MR imaging (6.3%). The CN-choroid plexus separation sign with CSF-equivalent signal reliably distinguishes it from cystic CPA mimics.

articles.title: Rebound of pediatric idiopathic ileocolic intussusception following the COVID-19 pandemic: a longitudinal follow-up study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Social distancing during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic was associated with a marked decline in pediatric idiopathic ileocolic intussusception, consistent with the well-known role of infection in this condition. Whether intussusception rates have rebounded following the lifting of pandemic-related restrictions remains unknown. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether the rate of pediatric idiopathic ileocolic intussusception returned to pre-pandemic levels after the relaxation of social distancing measures, using hypertrophic pyloric stenosis (HPS) as a control. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed air contrast enemas performed for idiopathic ileocolic intussusception at a single tertiary pediatric center from April 2016 through March 2026. Cases were categorized as pre-pandemic (April 2016-March 2020), pandemic (April 2020-March 2021), and post-pandemic (April 2022-March 2026). The 2021-2022 transitional year was excluded because the regional state of emergency ended during that interval, limiting its interpretability. Annualized case counts were compared across the prespecified periods using an exact conditional Poisson test with Garwood 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: In the pre-pandemic period, idiopathic ileocolic intussusception occurred at a mean of 31.5 cases/year (95% CI 26.2-37.5). During the pandemic, the rate decreased to a mean of 11 cases/year (95% CI 5.5-19.7), a 65% decrease (P<0.001). During the post-pandemic period, the mean rate was 38.5 cases/year (95% CI 32.7-45.1), a 250% increase relative to the pandemic period (P<0.001), and was not significantly different from the pre-pandemic rate (P=0.11), indicating a return to baseline. In contrast, HPS rates were 46.8 cases/year pre-pandemic (95% CI 40.3-54.0), 43 cases/year during the pandemic (95% CI 31.1-57.9), and 33.5 cases/year post-pandemic (95% CI 28.1-39.7), with no significant change from the pre-pandemic to the pandemic period (P=0.68) or from the pandemic to the post-pandemic period (P=0.16). A modest decline was observed when the post-pandemic period was compared to the pre-pandemic period (P=0.004). Across the study, the intussusception cohort comprised 126 male and 61 female patients (mean age 1.94 years, range 0.13-8 years) and the HPS cohort 140 male and 31 female patients (mean age 0.11 years, range 0.03-0.25 years). CONCLUSION: Idiopathic ileocolic intussusception demonstrated a statistically significant decline during the COVID-19 pandemic and rebounded to baseline in the post-pandemic period. The decline and subsequent recovery of intussusception temporally coincided with the imposition and relaxation of social distancing measures.

articles.title: The Importance of Molecular Imaging Response Criteria: Rationale and Overview.
articles.abstract: Assessment of therapeutic response in oncology is fundamental for evaluating treatment efficacy, guiding clinical decision-making, and determining prognosis. Historically, response evaluation relied primarily on anatomical imaging criteria derived from tumor size changes on computed tomography (CT), most notably the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) and its adaptations. However, advances in molecular imaging, particularly positron emission tomography (PET) using [18F]-2-fluoro-2-deoxyglucose ([18F]FDG) and other radiopharmaceuticals, have introduced new biomarkers capable of detecting tumor response earlier than structural changes. Molecular imaging-based criteria, including EORTC, PERCIST, immune-adapted PET frameworks, and disease-specific systems such as Lugano, RANO, ENETS SSTR-PeRForm and RECIP, provide quantitative assessment of tumor burden and may better reflect biologic response to therapy. This review discusses the rationale behind molecular imaging response criteria, outlines the principles of CT-based and PET-based evaluation systems, and highlights the clinical relevance of integrating metabolic imaging into tumor response.

articles.title: Rotating Frame Spin-Lock Cardiac MRI Method at 9.4 T Can Characterize Diffuse Fibrosis in Progressing Hypertensive Heart Disease in Mice.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the applicability of rotating frame spin-lock continuous wave (CW) T1ρ and relaxation along a fictitious field with Rank 2 (RAFF2) methods complementary to native T1 and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) for cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI) of diffuse fibrosis in mice with advancing hypertensive heart disease (HHD) and diastolic dysfunction. METHODS: HHD was induced in mice with angiotensin II infusion for 28 days; sham operated were used as controls. Phenotype progression was assessed with echocardiography. Characterization of diffuse fibrosis was performed with CMRI. CW-T1ρ and RAFF2 were compared with native T1 and LGE acquired on Days 14 and 28 of the experiment. Regions of interest in CMRI relaxation time maps and Picrosirius red-stained histological cardiac sections were compared. RESULTS: Diffuse fibrosis in the left ventricle was visible on Day 14 with TRAFF2 relaxation time maps in the HHD group with early diastolic impairment, and CW-T1ρ showed a slight increase. Both CW-T1ρ and TRAFF2 showed elevated values on Day 28 in HHD mice, whereas native T1 showed an increase only on Day 28. LGE showed no accumulation. The presence of diffuse fibrosis was verified with cardiac histology. CONCLUSIONS: Rotating frame spin-lock CW-T1ρ and RAFF2 are more sensitive to native T1 and LGE in the characterization of diffuse fibrosis in advancing HHD in mice, being an alternative for the imaging of fibrotic remodeling also in other cardiac pathologies.

articles.title: Generalizability of Deep Learning Architectures for Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Classification in Histopathology: A Comparative CNN-Vision Transformer Study with External Validation and Label-Quality Analysis.
articles.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is the most prevalent oral malignancy, with delayed diagnosis contributing to poor survival. Deep learning has shown promise for histopathological detection of OSCC, but reported performance is frequently based on single-source datasets, with limited external validation and variable annotation quality. Our study was to compare representative CNN and transformer architectures for histopathological OSCC classification and assess their generalizability under external domain shift. A total of 10,817 H&E-stained image patches from 114 patients were classified as OSCC or normal/control. Images were independently reviewed by two oral pathologists, with discordant cases adjudicated by a senior pathologist (Cohen's κ = 0.975). Eight ImageNet-pre-trained architectures (ResNet18, ResNet50, ResNet101, DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B0, ConvNeXt-Tiny, ViT-B/16, and Swin-T) were fine-tuned using three random seeds. Models were trained, validated, and tested on the internally curated dataset {MIDAS} and subsequently evaluated on two independent external datasets used exclusively for external validation. Diagnostic performance, computational efficiency, statistical significance, and model interpretability were assessed. To investigate the observed reduction in external performance, cancer-labelled images from the external datasets underwent post hoc expert pathological review for potential label discordance. A total of 10,817 H&E-stained image patches from 114 patients were classified as OSCC or normal/control. Images were independently reviewed by two oral pathologists, with discordant cases adjudicated by a senior pathologist (Cohen's κ = 0.975). Eight ImageNet-pre-trained architectures (ResNet18, ResNet50, ResNet101, DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B0, ConvNeXt-Tiny, ViT-B/16, and Swin-T) were fine-tuned using three random seeds. Models were evaluated on a patient-level internal test set and two independent external datasets. Diagnostic performance, computational efficiency, statistical differences, and interpretability were assessed. Cancer-labelled images from External Dataset 2 were post hoc reassessed for label discordance. ConvNeXt-Tiny demonstrated the strongest overall performance. Substantial external degradation across models highlights the effects of domain shift and label quality, emphasizing expert annotation, independent validation, reproducible benchmarking, and multi-institutional datasets for clinical translation.

articles.title: CSNet: Cognitive Simulation Network for Reliable Histopathology-Based Cancer Diagnosis.
articles.abstract: Histopathology-based cancer diagnosis is crucial for early detection and timely therapeutic intervention. However, most deep learning methods for histopathological image classification are mainly optimized as prediction models, with limited consideration of clinical diagnostic workflows. In routine practice, pathologists usually follow a sequential reasoning process: coarse assessment of possible abnormalities, detailed inspection of suspicious regions, and consultation-based reasoning to reduce uncertainty. To provide more reliable and interpretable decision support for histopathology-based cancer diagnosis, we propose the cognitive simulation network (CSNet), which draws inspiration from pathologists' sequential diagnostic workflow. First, the multi-view fuzzy assessment module integrates frequency, texture, and gradient cues through learnable fuzzy membership functions to estimate view-level abnormality degrees, providing an initial assessment of suspicious pathological evidence. Guided by this assessment, the gradient-guided fuzzy modulator converts abnormality information into spatial guidance, enhancing informative high-gradient morphological responses while suppressing redundant low-informative regions. Based on the modulated representations, the uncertainty-guided multi-expert synergy mechanism estimates diagnostic uncertainty and coordinates multiple expert branches to generate consensus representations for reliable prediction. Extensive experiments on Kather-5 K, LC25000, LC25000-clean, and a collected cervical cancer histopathology dataset demonstrate that CSNet achieves superior performance, with accuracies of 97.673%, 99.964%, 97.920%, and 99.861%, respectively. Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of the proposed designs, and statistical analyses confirm the reliability of the observed improvements. Meanwhile, robustness evaluations and comparative visualizations demonstrate stable performance and more consistent responses in diagnostically relevant tissue regions, highlighting the potential of CSNet for reliable histopathology-based cancer diagnosis.

articles.title: Semi-Automated Image Labeling and Object Tracking for MR-Guided Radiotherapy Using a Foundation Vision Model.
articles.abstract: Magnetic resonance-guided radiotherapy (MRgRT) enables real-time tracking of tumor and organ motion for more precise radiation delivery. However, existing clinical tracking software struggles with high-velocity or non-rigid motion. Foundation models, such as Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) and MedSAM2, offer robust tracking with fast inference speeds and strong zero-shot accuracy that can improve with fine-tuning. Fine-tuning typically uses expert-labeled datasets, which are expensive to acquire. We explored SAM2's utility in accelerating the labeling process by developing a workflow where novices label < 1% of frames and SAM2 automatically labels the rest. We then evaluated SAM2 and MedSAM2 for tumor tracking on an open-access MRgRT dataset in three configurations: zero-shot, fine-tuned using manually labeled data, and fine-tuned using the semi-automatically labeled data. We measured accuracy with the Dice similarity coefficient, 95th percentile (P95) Hausdorff distance, and centroid distance. MedSAM2 and SAM2 demonstrated strong zero-shot tracking accuracy with no significant difference among the model variants. Fine-tuning significantly improved Dice coefficients (0.874 to 0.891, p = 0.006), P95 Hausdorff distances (9.069 to 4.378 mm, p < 0.001), and centroid distances (5.299 to 1.769 mm, p < 0.001) relative to zero-shot, with no significant difference between using manually labeled and semi-automatically labeled data. Therefore, leveraging SAM2 to semi-automatically generate labeled training data can substantially reduce the cost of data curation and long-term model maintenance without compromising accuracy.

articles.title: From Intra- to Inter-habitat Analysis: Spatial Structure Features for Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis Prediction on Breast DCE-MRI.
articles.abstract: Habitat radiomics characterizes texture within tumor subregions but discards the spatial relationships between them. We developed a landscape-ecology-inspired framework quantifying inter-habitat spatial structure on DCE-MRI, evaluated its complementary value alongside within-habitat radiomics, and compared early versus late fusion, using axillary lymph node metastasis (ALNM) prediction as the evaluation task. In this multicenter retrospective study, 284 patients from one center were randomly split into training (n = 198) and validation (n = 86) cohorts, with 120 patients from an independent institution as the external test set. Tumors were partitioned into six habitats by k-means clustering of 19 voxel-wise texture descriptors, with centroids derived exclusively from the training cohort. Three feature domains were constructed: 8 clinical parameters, 642 within-habitat radiomics features, and 94 inter-habitat spatial structure features spanning fragmentation (n = 30), morphology (n = 24), inter-habitat contact (n = 15), inter-habitat distance (n = 15), area ratio (n = 6), and diversity (n = 4). In the external test set, progressive fusion yielded incremental gains in AUC: clinical alone 0.754, plus within-habitat radiomics 0.843, plus inter-habitat spatial structure 0.863 (95% CI 0.792-0.934). The full early fusion model achieved higher AUC than the clinical-only (DeLong P = 0.011) and spatial-structure-only models (P = 0.044); early fusion yielded a numerically higher AUC than late fusion without reaching significance (0.863 vs 0.851, P = 0.636). The two single-domain imaging models were statistically indistinguishable (0.817 vs 0.784, P = 0.512). Inter-habitat spatial structure captures tumor organization overlooked by conventional habitat radiomics and provides complementary information for preoperative ALNM prediction.

articles.title: Development and External Testing of an Interpretable MRI-Based Machine Learning Model for Differentiating Endometrial Stromal Sarcoma from Cellular Leiomyoma.
articles.abstract: This retrospective two-center diagnostic study was aimed at developing and externally testing an interpretable MRI-based machine learning model for differentiating endometrial stromal sarcoma (ESS) from cellular leiomyoma (CL). A total of 155 women with pathologically confirmed ESS or CL were assigned to a derivation cohort (n = 111) and an external testing cohort (n = 44). Clinical variables, qualitative MRI features, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) histogram parameters were evaluated. Three MRI-derived predictors-irregular tumor margin, cystic areas on T2-weighted imaging, and mean ADC-were used to train six classifiers. The final support vector machine model with a radial basis function kernel was evaluated at a fixed threshold determined in the derivation cohort using receiver operating characteristic, calibration, decision curve, and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analyses. A reader study assessed the effect of model assistance. The model achieved areas under the curve of 0.843 (95% CI, 0.760-0.917) in the derivation cohort and 0.835 (95% CI, 0.669-0.960) in the external testing cohort. Calibration and decision curve analyses indicated acceptable performance and potential clinical utility. In an exploratory model-assisted reader analysis, junior radiologist specificity increased from 46.4 to 82.1% and accuracy from 52.3 to 77.3%. This interpretable three-feature model demonstrated promising performance across cohorts and may serve as an adjunctive tool for preoperative MRI assessment, although prospective multicenter validation is warranted.

articles.title: Interpretable Source-Aware Bone-Muscle Fusion Framework for Multicenter Prediction of Osteoporotic Vertebral Fractures.
articles.abstract: Osteoporotic vertebral fracture (OVF) is underrecognized, and bone mineral density (BMD) alone may be insufficient for prediction.
